topics.title: Meaning, Principles, and Suitability of Job Costing
explain: Job Costing is a costing method used where work consists of separate contracts, jobs, or batches, each executed to specific customer orders.
Each job or unit of production is treated as a separate costing entity to ascertain its cost and profitability.
It is applicable when no two orders are alike and each job requires individual customized treatment.
Commonly used in industries like printing, furniture making, hardware, shipbuilding, repair shops, and heavy machinery.

flow.title: How Job Costing Operates
steps: Customer places custom order
Assign unique job order number
Track direct costs for the job
Apply overheads to the job
Determine total cost and profit

topics.example: A printing press printing customized wedding invitation cards based on specific design requests from individual clients.
remember: Batch production is similar to job costing, differing mainly in the size of the orders.
mistakes: Assuming job costing is used for mass production of standardized identical products instead of custom orders.

quiz.q: Which costing method is most appropriate when products are manufactured according to specific customer specifications?
quiz.why: Job costing is designed specifically to trace costs to individual customized orders.

quiz.q: In job costing, each job or work order is treated as a:
quiz.why: Each job is tracked independently as a distinct cost unit to find its individual cost.

topics.title: Job Cost Card / Sheet and Process of Job Costing
explain: A Job Cost Sheet (or Job Cost Card) is a cost statement used to record all material, labour, and overhead expenditures for a specific job.
It contains details such as job number, description, blueprint number, material issues, employee hours spent, overheads applied, and profitability.
A separate cost sheet is opened as soon as a job order is received and initiated.
When the job is completed, overhead charges are added to ascertain the total expenditure.

flow.title: Process of Maintaining a Job Cost Sheet
steps: Open Job Cost Sheet on order receipt
Post direct materials from store requisitions
Log direct employee hours from time cards
Apply overhead charges upon completion
Calculate total cost and selling price

topics.example: A furniture workshop opening Job Cost Sheet #401 to track timber costs, carpenter hours, and varnish overheads for a custom office table.
remember: A Bill of Materials acts as the foundation for preparing store requisitions for a specific job.
mistakes: Confusing estimated cost columns with actual cost columns on the job cost summary sheet.

quiz.q: Which document is used to accumulate direct materials, labour hours, and overheads for a specific job?
quiz.why: The Job Cost Sheet is the primary document used to log all costs incurred on a specific job.

quiz.q: What document provides the basis for issuing stores requisitions for a given job?
quiz.why: The Bill of Material specifies all required materials for a job, enabling store requisition preparation.

topics.title: Collection of Costs for a Job
explain: Direct material costs are collected using separate stores requisitions priced and entered in a material abstract book before posting to the Work-in-Progress (WIP) ledger.
Surplus material returned to stores requires a Store Debit Note; direct transfers between jobs require a Material Transfer Note.
Direct labour costs are collected via job time cards, valued at hourly rates, summarized in a labour abstract book, and posted periodically to the WIP ledger.
Idle time costs and indirect wages are collected under standing order numbers and charged to Factory Overhead Control Account.
Manufacturing overheads are allocated to production departments and applied to jobs using rates such as machine hours or direct labour hours.

flow.title: Cost Collection and Posting Flow
steps: Issue materials via stores requisitions
Log employee time on job cards
Summarize in material & labour abstract books
Post summary totals to WIP cost sheets
Apply departmental overhead absorption rates

topics.example: When transferring leftover steel rods directly from Job #10 to Job #14, the foreman prepares a Material Transfer Note to adjust WIP accounts.
remember: Surplus material moved directly between jobs requires a Material Transfer Note, avoiding store returns.
mistakes: Debiting idle time directly to the specific job cost sheet instead of Factory Overhead Control Account.

quiz.q: Which document is prepared when surplus material is transferred directly from one job to another?
quiz.why: A Material Transfer Note records the direct transfer of materials between jobs so WIP accounts can be adjusted.

quiz.q: Worker idle time in job costing is generally booked against:
o: The specific job being worked on
Costing Profit and Loss Account directly
quiz.why: Idle time is an indirect labour cost charged to standing order numbers under factory overheads.

topics.title: Treatment of Spoiled and Defective Work
explain: Spoiled work is production totally rejected and non-rectifiable; defective work can be rectified by spending extra cost.
Normal spoilage/defects within allowed limits: cost of rectification or loss is charged to the specific job or spread across the batch.
Abnormal spoilage/defects exceeding limits: cost of rectification or loss is written off to Costing Profit and Loss Account.
Defects caused by bad workmanship are treated as abnormal costs and written off to Costing Profit & Loss, unless recovered as a penalty from the worker.
Defects due to Inspection Department accepting poor materials are charged to that department and written off to Costing P&L.

flow.title: Handling Defective and Spoiled Work
steps: Inspect finished batch for defect/spoilage
Determine if defect is normal or abnormal
If normal: charge rectification to job/batch
If abnormal: write off cost to Costing P&L

topics.example: In a batch of 100 gears, 2 defective gears are within the normal 2% limit, so their repair cost is added to the entire batch cost.
remember: Normal defective costs are absorbed by good units/batch; abnormal defective costs go straight to Costing P&L.
mistakes: Charging abnormal rectification costs caused by negligence to the job cost sheet instead of Costing P&L.

quiz.q: How is the cost of rectifying abnormal defective work due to bad workmanship treated?
o: Spread over all job cost sheets
Written off to Costing Profit & Loss Account
Debited to Stores Ledger Control Account
quiz.why: Abnormal costs arising from negligence or bad workmanship must be written off to Costing Profit & Loss Account.

quiz.q: Production that is completely rejected and cannot be rectified is called:
quiz.why: Spoiled work cannot be repaired, whereas defective work can be brought to perfection with extra expenditure.

topics.title: Accounting Entries in Control Accounts
explain: In non-integrated cost accounting, double-entry journal entries pass through control accounts using a Cost Ledger Control Account.
Issue of direct materials to jobs: Debit Work-in-Process (WIP) Control A/c, Credit Stores Ledger Control A/c.
Direct wages incurred on jobs: Debit WIP Control A/c, Credit Wages Control A/c.
Factory overhead applied to jobs: Debit WIP Control A/c, Credit Factory Overhead Control A/c.
Total cost of completed jobs: Debit Cost of Sales A/c, Credit WIP Control A/c.
Sales value of completed jobs: Debit Cost Ledger Control A/c, Credit Costing Profit and Loss A/c.

flow.title: Flow of Cost Control Entries
steps: Debit WIP Control for direct materials & labour
Debit WIP Control for absorbed overheads
Transfer completed jobs to Cost of Sales A/c
Transfer Cost of Sales balance to Costing P&L

topics.example: When ₹5,000 of direct wood is issued to Job #101, Work-in-Process Control A/c is debited and Stores Ledger Control A/c is credited.
remember: Direct expenses enter WIP Control A/c directly, while indirect expenses pass through Overhead Control A/c.
mistakes: Crediting Cost Ledger Control Account instead of Stores Ledger Control Account when issuing direct materials to a job.

quiz.q: Which account is debited when direct materials are issued to specific jobs?
quiz.why: Direct material costs increase work-in-progress, so Work-in-Process Control A/c is debited.

quiz.q: When overheads are absorbed into jobs, the journal entry is:
o: Dr. Factory Overhead Control, Cr. WIP Control
Dr. WIP Control, Cr. Factory Overhead Control
Dr. Cost of Sales, Cr. Factory Overhead Control
Dr. Costing P&L, Cr. WIP Control
quiz.why: Absorbed factory overhead increases the WIP asset balance, debiting WIP Control and crediting Factory Overhead Control.

topics.title: Advantages, Disadvantages & Job Costing vs Process Costing
explain: Advantages of Job Costing: provides detailed cost control per job, helps determine individual job profitability, assists in production planning and standard costing.
Disadvantages: involves extensive clerical work making it costly, higher risk of clerical errors, less effective during high inflation.
Job Costing tracks distinct, non-continuous, customized jobs against specific customer orders, computing costs when each job completes.
Process Costing tracks continuous flow of homogeneous identical products, compiling costs on a time-period basis per process/department.
In Job Costing products retain their individual identity; in Process Costing products lose their individual identity.

flow.title: Choosing Between Job Costing and Process Costing
steps: Assess product nature (Custom vs Standard)
If custom order: Apply Job Costing per job #
Compute cost upon job completion
If uniform continuous flow: Apply Process Costing
Compute average cost per time period

topics.example: Building a custom yacht uses Job Costing, whereas refining crude oil continuously into petrol uses Process Costing.
remember: Costs in job costing are computed when the job completes, whereas process costs are calculated per time period.
mistakes: Assuming job costing computes unit costs periodically by dividing total period costs by total output.

quiz.q: Which feature distinguishes Job Costing from Process Costing?
o: Job Costing is for continuous mass production
Costs are computed per period in Job Costing
Each job maintains its individual identity in Job Costing
Process Costing is used for customized customer orders
quiz.why: In Job Costing, each job order is unique and retains its identity, unlike continuous homogeneous processes.

quiz.q: What is a major limitation of the Job Costing method?
o: It cannot calculate profit for individual orders
It requires significant and costly clerical work
It can only be used in continuous assembly lines
It prevents the application of budgetary control
quiz.why: Detailed record-keeping for materials, labour, and overhead for every single job involves laborious clerical work.
